summary: Created “Fleet Internal CA” on node1, trusted it system-wide on both nodes, issued node2 a server certificate for DNS node2 and IP 10.100.205.11, and configured persistent HTTPS on TCP/8443. Both nodes were rebooted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot identities. RHEL 10 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were preserved.
actions_performed: Installed the supported RHEL OpenSSL package without replacing the operating-system release or kernel.
Created a protected 3072-bit CA key and ten-year CA certificate on node1.
Generated node2’s private key locally, signed only its CSR on node1, and installed the resulting server certificate securely.
Installed the CA into both RHEL system trust stores.
Configured a hardened, non-root systemd HTTPS service on node2 using the existing Python 3.12 runtime.
Opened only TCP/8443 in node2’s runtime and persistent firewalld configuration.
Verified successful trusted HTTPS by DNS and IP, correct certificate presentation, and rejection of an invalid hostname.
Removed temporary CSR/configuration artifacts and confirmed SELinux remained enforcing, SSH remained available, and no systemd units failed.
Rebooted node1 and node2 one at a time, proving changed boot IDs and complete recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA on node1
evidence.summary: Shows the exact CA subject and issuer, validity, fingerprint, valid protected key, system trust, secure permissions, and unchanged CA checksums after reboot.
Proves node2-local key generation, CA-side signing, server-auth usage, DNS/IP SANs, certificate/key match, and system-trust verification.

evidence.requirement: Install the CA as trusted on both nodes
evidence.summary: Both systems list Fleet Internal CA as a trusted authority; node2 validates its server certificate through the system CA bundle.

Shows the enabled service, persistent firewall rule and listener, successful trusted responses, correct Fleet Internal CA chain, wrong-host rejection, zero service restarts, and healthy final service state.

Initial and final evidence confirms RHEL 10, the unchanged installed kernel, SELinux enforcing, active SSH/firewalld, unchanged /etc/hosts checksums, no AVC denials, no temporary Fleet files, and zero failed units.

Healthy baseline boot ID 2b19e976-dee2-4700-9045-90d61b6dcffe, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot ID 31cf3662-4db0-40e1-a363-f3bb1eea9c04, and recovered CA/trust, SSH, firewall, data checksums, kernel, and HTTPS client behavior.

Healthy baseline boot ID 254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot ID 7d1ec017-4ea1-423e-bde7-da3a574dbce6, and recovered HTTPS, trust, certificate identity, firewall, SSH, protected data, SELinux enforcement, and zero failed units.
